title: gateway/metrics: classify streaming disconnects (client abort vs server-side)
author: Amara Diallo
release_notes: Adds streaming disconnect classification in API gateway metrics to separate client-initiated aborts from server-side disconnects; updates dashboards/SLI queries to use new labels.
description:
Context: For tiered SLOs we need a consistent definition of “streaming disconnect rate” for chat/completions streaming. Today we emit a single counter for “stream ended unexpectedly” but it mixes: (a) users navigating away / client cancels, (b) server-side disconnects (gateway timeout, upstream reset), and (c) transport errors (HTTP/2 stream reset). This has been causing noisy/incorrect burn during customer-reported “disconnect” spikes (SUP-3924) and makes it hard to align with the SLI spec (ENG-2428).

What this PR does: Introduces a structured disconnect classification for streaming responses in the API gateway and updates our metrics emission so we can separate client abort vs server-side disconnect. The new metrics are designed to be low-cardinality and compatible with tier/region/model/route dimensions already propagated through request context.

Changes: 1) Adds `gateway_stream_disconnect_total` counter with label `reason` (enum) and `stage` (where the disconnect was observed). 2) Adds `gateway_stream_disconnect_classification_total` (temporary parallel counter) to validate classification before we cut dashboards over; will be removed after ~2 weeks. 3) Updates existing `gateway_stream_ended_total{status=...}` to stop treating 499/ctx-cancel as gateway fault. 4) Adds a small helper to normalize Go net/http errors + gRPC upstream errors into the enum. 5) Adds tests that simulate client cancel, upstream reset, gateway deadline exceeded, and write errors.

Classification: - `client_abort`: client closed connection / request context canceled and we did not observe an upstream error first. - `upstream_reset`: upstream (routing/runtime) closed/reset stream before natural EOF; includes HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and gRPC CANCELLED observed from upstream. - `gateway_timeout`: gateway enforced deadline (stream exceeded configured max duration or idle timeout). - `gateway_write_error`: gateway write failed (broken pipe) without explicit client cancel signal (rare, but shows up as EPIPE). - `unknown`: fallback bucket when we cannot classify (should be <0.5%).

Notes/constraints: - We do NOT add raw error strings as labels. Only the small enum to keep cardinality bounded. - We preserve the existing route/model/tier/region dimensions (already in request context) so SRE can slice by tier. - For now, we keep `unknown` to avoid dropping events; we’ll tune after validation.

Rollout plan: - Ship behind config `gateway.metrics.streaming_disconnect_classification=true` (defaults on in staging, off in prod). - Once we validate on staging and a small prod canary, update SLI queries/dashboards to use `reason != client_abort` as “server-side disconnects” for burn. - After 2 weeks, delete the temporary validation counter.

Validation: - Compared old vs new counters on staging for 24h; total disconnect counts match within 1.3% (difference mostly due to previously double-counting certain ctx-cancel paths). - Spot-checked a handful of incident traces (from the SUP-3924 timeframe) and confirmed most “disconnect spikes” were client_abort.

Links: - Linear ENG-2428 (Streaming disconnect classification) - Linear ENG-2418 (Hosted SLIs) - Jira SUP-3924 (Hosted streaming disconnect complaints)
commits: gateway/stream: thread disconnect classification through stream handler lifecycle
tests: add integration-style tests for client cancel vs upstream reset vs timeout
dashboards: add temporary panels for old vs new disconnect counters (staging only)
conversation: Aisha Bello (review): Can we be explicit about how we distinguish client_abort vs gateway_write_error? My concern is that we’ll still classify broken pipe as server-side and that’ll skew the streaming disconnect SLI. Also, please confirm how 499 is handled across our proxy chain.

Amara Diallo (author): Good call. In Go we get EPIPE/ECONNRESET on write for both client closes and some intermediate resets. I updated the classifier to prefer ctx cancellation / CloseNotify signal as client_abort when present, even if the subsequent write returns EPIPE. Only classify gateway_write_error when ctx is still active and we fail to write. 499 from downstream clients isn’t directly visible here (we’re the edge), but we’ll treat `context.Canceled` / downstream close as client_abort. Added a note in gateway/observability/metrics.md.

Nadia Rahman (review): +1 on keeping cardinality low. Can we confirm we’re not adding model_id as a label here (we already have model in some places). Also, do we need the temporary `gateway_stream_disconnect_classification_total`? I’d rather not keep two counters long-term.

Amara Diallo (author): Agreed. No new high-card labels in this PR; it uses the existing request tags that are already bounded by our propagation rules. The temporary counter is only for validation while dashboards still depend on the old metric; I’ll add a TODO with a deadline and link ENG-2428 so we delete it after cutover.

Logan Wright (review): The enum names should be stable and documented since they’ll end up in queries/alerts. Please add documentation + ensure we emit `unknown` rather than dropping when classification fails. Also: stage label—what are the possible values?

Amara Diallo (author): Added docs in gateway/observability/metrics.md and in code comments. `stage` values are `before_upstream_headers`, `after_upstream_headers`, `during_body` (coarse-grained; no error strings). Default to `during_body` if we can’t tell. Unknown is emitted explicitly.
Ethan Park (review): Can we gate this by config so we can enable in staging first? Also please confirm it won’t affect request handling (no extra locks in hot path).

Amara Diallo (author): Yep—behind `gateway.metrics.streaming_disconnect_classification`. Implementation is purely local bookkeeping; no additional locks, and classification runs only on stream end. I also moved a small allocation out of the per-chunk loop.
Aisha Bello (follow-up): Thanks. One more request: add a short snippet in the description about how SRE should compute server-side disconnect SLI (exclude client_abort).
Amara Diallo (author): Done—added guidance in metrics.md and included a sample PromQL query comment in the dashboard jsonnet.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved. This unblocks the SLI spec writeup for streaming disconnects.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved after docs + TODO. Please remember to remove the parallel counter after validation.
